prompt_text: Who is the best real estate agent in Pleasanton CA to sell my house?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” agent for everyone — the right agent depends on your home type, price range, timeline and what matters most to you (marketing, top dollar, fast sale, low stress). I can help you find the best fit. To get started, tell me a few quick details, or use the checklist and questions below to vet agents yourself.

Quick questions so I can recommend candidates:
- Property address or neighborhood in Pleasanton
- Estimated list price or price range
- Desired time frame to sell
- Any preferences (single agent vs. team, commission flexibility, staging help, experience with luxury homes, investors, etc.)

How to identify the top agents in Pleasanton
- Look for recent local track record: number of homes sold in Pleasanton in the last 12 months, average list-to-sale price ratio, and average days on market.
- Compare agents’ marketing: professional photos, floor plans, virtual tours, targeted online ads, open houses and neighborhood-specific outreach.
- Read reviews and ask for client references for similar homes/neighborhoods.
- Check local MLS sales data and county records (most reliable for performance).
- Prefer agents who are active in your specific submarket (e.g., Downtown Pleasanton, Vintage Hills, Fairlands).

Key metrics to ask for
- How many Pleasanton homes have you sold in the last 12 months?
- Average sold price vs. list price for those homes
- Average days on market
- Number of buyers they personally represented vs. listings (shows negotiation experience)
- Percentage of their business that’s repeat/referral clients

Interview questions to ask potential agents
- What is your marketing plan for a home like mine?
- What comparable sales would you use to price my home?
- How will you stage/prepare the home? Do you offer staging or vendor discounts?
- How will you communicate updates and how often?
- Can you provide 3 recent references from Pleasanton sellers?
- What is your commission and are there any additional fees?
- If the home doesn’t sell in X days, what is your plan?

Red flags
- Vague or no marketing plan
- Refusal to provide references or concrete recent comps
- Unrealistic price guarantees or pressures to accept a quick low offer
- Poor reviews complaining about communication or unexpected fees

If you want, I can:
- Draft an outreach/email template to contact agents
- Help evaluate agent responses side-by-side
- Suggest specific agent names (if you provide the address and let me search current listings and sales data)

Tell me which option you prefer and share the property details if you want personalized recommendations.
